blocks.content: The primary objective of FCI is to safeguard the interests of farmers through remunerative procurement and ensure food security via equitable distribution.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Food Corporation of India (FCI) was established under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, to implement the National Food Policy.
FCI provides price support operations to safeguard farmers from distress sales through Minimum Support Price (MSP) purchases.
It maintains strategic buffer stocks of food grains to stabilize market prices and ensure national food security during distress.
FCI distributes essential food grains across all states and Union Territories through the Public Distribution System (PDS) and Targeted PDS (TPDS).

rows: Ensure remunerative returns and prevent distress selling
Ensure affordable access to staple grains for vulnerable groups
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (based on CACP recommendations)
Central Government (as framed under the National Food Security Act)
Forms the primary procurement cost for FCI
Drives the annual Food Subsidy burden (Economic Cost minus CIP)

items: FCI functions under the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Government of India.
While CACP recommends the Minimum Support Price (MSP), FCI acts as the primary agency responsible for procuring grains at MSP.
Food Subsidy is calculated as the difference between the Economic Cost of food grains to FCI and the Central Issue Price (CIP).
